The paper was published in Advanced Materials Research Vols. 123-125 (2010) by Jin-Bong Kim and Chun-Gon Kim from Korea Institute of Materials Science and Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology.
The study focuses on designing 2-layer Dällenbach type radar absorbers using E-glass/epoxy composite laminates with carbon nanotube dispersions.
CNT weight percentages tested ranged from 1.5 to 4.0 wt%, with the optimal design case using 5.27 wt% CNT.
The absorber was designed for 10 GHz (center frequency of X-band: 8.2-12.4 GHz) with design cases exploring 5.0-15.0 GHz frequency ranges.
Complex permittivity was measured across 0.5-18.0 GHz using a coaxial air line and vector network analyzer.
The nominal lamina thickness was approximately 0.111 ± 0.02 mm, increasing proportionally with CNT content.
Resin content (R/C) of cured laminates was approximately 43 wt%.
E-glass fabric specifications: plain weave type with 60 and 57 yarns/in in warp and fill directions, fiber aerial weight of 107 g/m².
Composite curing was performed at 80°C for 30 minutes followed by 120°C for over 2 hours in an autoclave.
Five design optimization cases (CASE1-CASE5) were analyzed with varying frequency bands and LIM (limit) values.
CASE1 design parameters: first layer thickness 2.91 mm, second layer thickness 1.44 mm, CNT content 5.27 wt%.
The fabricated CASE1 absorber had first layer of 32 plies (2.88 mm) and second layer of 11 plies (1.40 mm).
Measured -10 dB absorbing bandwidth of the fabricated absorber was 7.4 GHz with total thickness of 4.28 mm.
The reflection loss curve exhibits two peaks, and the width between peaks must be optimized for broad-band absorption.
Genetic algorithm was used as the optimization method with an objective function minimizing reflection loss across target frequency bands.
The complex permittivity of CNT-composites was semi-empirically modeled as functions of frequency and CNT content.
CNT (CM-95) was provided by Hanwha Nanotech of Korea and mixed with diluted BPA-type epoxy and acid anhydride hardener.
Acetone was used to dilute the epoxy resin to achieve low viscosity for higher CNT concentration, then easily evaporated during prepreg drying.
Microstructural observations showed that CNT particles are distributed primarily in the resin-rich areas between E-glass fabrics.
Discrepancies between designed and measured results were attributed to discrete laminate thickness (integer multiples of ply thickness) and variations in measured permittivity.
The study demonstrated that fiber reinforcement prevents agglomeration of nano fillers during high-temperature curing, maintaining uniform property distribution.
The research was supported by the New & Renewable Energy R&D program under the Korea Ministry of Knowledge Economy.
The transmission line method was used to calculate reflection coefficients and design multi-layer absorbers.
Characteristic impedance and propagation constant depend on permittivity and permeability of the media.
For dielectric absorbers, permeability is assumed to be unity (μ = 1).
